points.description: States the answer is FALSE (the statement is not correct).
Justifies that the OS can still schedule/switch processes without the timer interrupt, e.g. on system calls (or other events like I/O, blocking, yield, process exit), though not necessarily fairly.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says the OS can still switch/schedule without the timer (e.g. cooperative/other events) but gives no clear example or is vague.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says FALSE and explains that the OS can still switch processes on other events such as system calls (I/O, yield, exit), even if less fair. Part marks: FALSE with a vague or incomplete reason that is on the right track. No marks if the answer says TRUE or gives no correct justification.
